description: Crater-basin uranium: uranium carried by oxidised groundwater and fixed in the reduced, organic-rich sediments and breccias that fill an impact structure.

source.note: inside the rim of an impact structure at least 5 km across: a closed basin with fractured, permeable rock under it

driver.note: the basin is filling with sediment (lake beds, reworked ejecta); design thresholds

trap.note: porous beds for the groundwater to move through (design)

notes: P2-08 (meteor impacts). Uranium in impact structures: the Cluff Lake deposits in the Carswell structure, Saskatchewan (39 km; unconformity-type ore brought up and reworked by the central uplift), and uranium in the crater-fill and breccias of other structures (Grieve & Masaitis 1994 (The economic potential of terrestrial impact craters, Int. Geol. Rev. 36(2):105-151); Grieve 2005, Geol. Soc. London Spec. Publ. 248:1-29). Uranium moves only in oxidised water, hence the clock.

PLACEHOLDERS (design values, no USGS grade-tonnage or deposit-density model exists for impact deposits; crates/deeptime-core/data/usgs/impact_structures.json): tonnage, grades, ore density, deposit density, separation, clustering, geometry and the curves' thresholds.

Crater-basin oil is not a type of its own: the impact stage adds the closure of crater rims and central uplifts to deeptime:trap_structure, impact breccia is a reservoir rock, and deeptime:petroleum_trap names the impact among its trap causes.
